angler_note: Indicates plankton productivity. Higher = more baitfish and predators, but extreme blooms may reduce oxygen.
Fish need oxygen to thrive; best fishing in 4–10 mg/L. Very high often means mixing after storms.
Nutrients fuel productivity. Balanced levels support good food chains, extreme highs may trigger blooms.
Another key nutrient. Balanced levels mean good fishing waters, very high can signal eutrophication.
Normal sea salinity (~35 PSU) is best for most marine fish; low salinity favours estuary species.
Temperature drives seasonal activity. 10–18°C suits mixed fisheries; warmer waters favour bass, tuna, mackerel.
Like chlorophyll, it signals food chain strength. Higher levels attract baitfish and predators.
